slides.text: Working as the game master for 'Captain Blackbeard’s Cursed Brig' paid twelve dollars an hour, and Tyler took the responsibility with grave, solemn dignity. He dimmed the lights, put on his pirate tricorn hat, and watched the security cameras as the 7:00 PM booking entered: four senior structural engineers from MIT out for a corporate team-building retreat. Tyler cleared his throat into the intercom to deliver his ominous pirate riddle. He never got the chance.

Instead of searching for the plastic skull key hidden inside the sea chest, the engineers produced digital calipers and laser levels from their backpacks. In under four minutes, they deduced that the faux-wood wall paneling was non-load-bearing, neatly unscrewed the ventilation grate with a pocket multi-tool, and bypassed the pirate puzzle entirely. Tyler frantically tapped his microphone, shouting that they were breaking maritime law, but the engineers were already tracing electrical conduits behind the drywall.

Ten minutes later, the engineers burst through an unmarked service door into the mall's utility corridor—holding a dusty metal ledger they had uncovered inside a hollowed-out pillar. When the mall manager arrived, the engineers were at the front desk, highlighting sixty-four discrepancies in the landlord’s 2021 commercial property tax filings. Tyler sat in his pirate hat, weeping quietly over his unused treasure map, while the engineers gave the escape room a three-star Yelp review for 'inadequate fire suppression.'
